intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

experiences.name: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market where you can taste local cheeses, olives, cured meats, spices, and fresh produce alongside locals. A guided or self-guided walk through the stalls offers an authentic culinary immersion away from the heat.

experiences.name: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach
experiences.description: Visit the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon and evening when temperatures drop. Swim in the crystal-clear waters of the Saronic Gulf, enjoy sunbeds, and watch the spectacular Athenian Riviera sunset. Easily accessible from central Athens and close to quality seafood restaurants.

experiences.name: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine
experiences.description: Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district, learning to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and tzatziki from scratch. Classes run in the evening to avoid heat, and you enjoy your creations as dinner afterward.

experiences.name: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island
experiences.description: Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon, avoiding peak heat. Swim at the calm, clear beaches near Aegina Town, try the island's famous pistachio products and fresh fish at a harbor taverna, and return by evening ferry. A full island experience within budget and close to Athens.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Explore the atmospheric streets, browse souvenir stalls, and soak in your first views of the Acropolis lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near the airport or on arrival in Athens (€2–3)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna in Psiri — try souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and a Greek salad for around €8–10. Look for spots packed with locals rather than tourists.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is short due to afternoon arrival. Prioritize rest and orientation. Buy a rechargeable Ath.ena transit card at the airport Metro station for cheaper travel around Athens.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (Acropolis + surrounding sites) costs €30 but is well worth it — valid for 5 days across multiple sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for budget souvenirs and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Thissio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the pedestrian promenade. Enjoy the golden hour atmosphere before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) or spanakopita from a local bakery near your hostel — €1.50–2
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyros wrap from a street stand near Monastiraki (€2.50–3.50)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna dinner in Thissio or Psiri — moussaka or pastitsio with a carafe of house wine, around €10–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Acropolis involves uneven marble surfaces. Bring water and sunscreen. The combined Acropolis ticket saves money if you plan to visit multiple ancient sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums) — entry is €12. Spend 2–3 hours exploring ancient Greek artifacts, the Antikythera Mechanism, and stunning gold Mycenaean treasures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian quarter with street art, independent cafes, and a very local vibe. Visit the colorful Strefi Hill park for panoramic city views at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Kolonaki, Athens' upscale neighborhood, for window shopping and people-watching. Take the Lycabettus Hill funicular (€7 return) for spectacular 360° views of Athens and the Acropolis at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor — €0.50, plus Greek coffee at a local kafeneio (€1.50)
meals.lunch: Eat at a laiki (street market) if one is running nearby, or find a neighborhood psistaria (grill house) for a budget plate — €6–8
meals.dinner: Try fasolada (bean soup) or gemista (stuffed vegetables) at a traditional ouzeri in Exarchia — filling and very affordable at €7–9

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays — check the day of the week and adjust if needed. Exarchia is lively and authentic but stay aware of your surroundings in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early Metro + tram to Glyfada or Vouliagmeni beach on the Athens Riviera — about 45–60 minutes from central Athens. Vouliagmeni has a stunning natural lake (€15 entry) or free public beach sections nearby. Enjoy a morning swim in the clear Aegean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at the beach or explore the coastal promenade. Rent a sunbed if desired (€5–8) or bring your own towel and find a free spot. The water temperature in June is perfect — around 22–24°C.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by tram/Metro. Head to the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) area in the evening for a lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from a bakery before heading out — cheese pie and juice, €2–3
meals.lunch: Beach taverna lunch — grilled fish of the day or calamari with salad and bread, €12–15 (a slight splurge for the beach experience)
meals.dinner: Eat at a no-frills taverna near the Central Market — fresh grilled sardines or a mixed meze plate, €8–10

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera beaches are easily accessible by public transport — take Metro Line 2 to Syntagma then the tram toward Voula/Vouliagmeni. Bring cash as some beach vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early morning ferry from Piraeus port to Aegina island — one of the closest and most affordable Greek islands (ferry ticket €8–10 each way, journey ~1 hour). Arrive and rent a bicycle (€5–8/day) to explore the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to the stunning Temple of Aphaia (€6 entry) — one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples with panoramic sea views. Then head to Agia Marina beach on the east coast for a refreshing swim in turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegina Town in the late afternoon. Browse the colorful harbor, try local pistachios (Aegina is famous for them — buy a bag for €3–5), then catch the evening ferry back to Piraeus.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing or grab something at Piraeus port — coffee and pastry, €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a harbor taverna in Aegina Town — grilled octopus or fish soup with bread, €10–13
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — grab a souvlaki wrap or eat at your hostel's communal kitchen to save money after a full day, €3–5

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance at the Blue Star Ferries or Hellenic Seaways websites. The first ferry from Piraeus is usually around 7:00–8:00 AM. Piraeus is reachable from central Athens via Metro Line 1 (Green Line).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the KTEL bus from Athens (Kifissos Bus Terminal) to Nafplio in the Peloponnese — about 2.5 hours, ticket ~€13. Check into a budget guesthouse in Nafplio's charming old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful Venetian old town on foot — one of Greece's most picturesque towns. Visit the Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) by climbing the famous 999 steps for breathtaking views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront promenade and through the neoclassical streets of the old town. Watch the sunset from Acronauplia (the lower castle, free to walk around).

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing Athens or at the bus terminal — coffee and koulouri, €2
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite after arriving in Nafplio — gyros or a cheese pie from a local bakery, €3–4
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional taverna in Nafplio's old town — try the local specialty of lamb with orzo (arni me kritharaki), €10–12

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is a great base for exploring the Peloponnese. Book your guesthouse in advance as it's a popular destination. The Palamidi steps are steep — go in the morning or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi (€10–15 shared) to Epidaurus to visit the ancient Theatre of Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world with remarkable acoustics. Entry is €12 (combined with the museum).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and head to Karathona Beach — a lovely sandy beach just a 20-minute walk from the old town (or short taxi ride). Enjoy the calm, clear waters of the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Nafplio for a leisurely evening. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar with Acropolis views (just a drink — budget €4–6 for a local beer or wine).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse if included, or a local bakery — tiropita and coffee, €2.50
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the local market — olives, feta, bread, tomatoes, and fruit — €4–5 total
meals.dinner: Try a psarotaverna (fish taverna) near the waterfront — grilled sea bream or sea bass with vegetables, €12–14

day_by_day.notes: Epidaurus also hosts a famous summer festival of ancient drama — check if any performances coincide with your visit (tickets from €15). The beach at Karathona is free with no facilities, so bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Nafplio to Santorini: Take the KTEL bus back to Athens (or to Piraeus directly), then board an afternoon high-speed ferry to Santorini. Alternatively, take a direct ferry from Nafplio area ports. High-speed ferry from Piraeus to Santorini takes ~5 hours (€40–55 economy).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini (Thira) at the port of Athinios. Take the local bus (€1.80) up to Fira, the island's capital. Check into a budget hostel or studio apartment in Fira or nearby Karterados (cheaper than Oia).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Fira on foot — walk along the caldera edge for stunning views, browse the main street, and get oriented on the island.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — bakery items, €2–3
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or pack snacks for the journey — sandwiches and fruit, €3–5
meals.dinner: First dinner in Santorini — find a local taverna away from the main tourist strip in Fira for more reasonable prices. Try fava (yellow split pea dip) and tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), local Santorini specialties, €10–12

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is the most expensive part of this itinerary. Save money by staying in Fira or Karterados rather than Oia, eating at local spots away from the caldera-view restaurants, and using the island's public bus system (KTEL Santorini) instead of taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Perissa or Perivolos beach on the south coast — famous for their black volcanic sand. Arrive early to claim a good spot. The beach is free; sunbeds cost €5–8 if desired.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the beach. The black sand gets very hot in the afternoon sun — bring sandals. Swim in the crystal-clear blue Aegean. Walk along the long beach promenade connecting Perissa and Perivolos.
day_by_day.evening: Take the bus back to Fira. Walk the famous caldera path from Fira toward Imerovigli for spectacular sunset views — this is free and arguably better than the crowded Oia sunset spot.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry from a local bakery in Fira before heading to the beach — €2.50
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perissa — fresh calamari, Greek salad, and a cold Mythos beer, €12–15
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira at a non-caldera-view restaurant — souvlaki plate or moussaka, €9–11. The caldera-view restaurants charge 2–3x more for the same food.

day_by_day.notes: The black sand beaches of Santorini are unique but the sand gets extremely hot — water shoes or sandals are essential. Perissa has more budget-friendly options than the northern beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€15–25/day) to explore the island independently. Drive to the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by volcanic ash (entry €12). Often called the 'Greek Pompeii.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Red Beach near Akrotiri — one of Santorini's most dramatic and unique beaches with towering red volcanic cliffs. Then continue to the village of Megalochori or Pyrgos for a more authentic, less touristy Santorini experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive up to Pyrgos village (the highest point on the island) for panoramic 360° views and a quieter sunset experience than Oia. Explore the medieval castle ruins at the top.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or a local cafe — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, €3–4
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch bought from a local mini-market — bread, local Santorini cherry tomatoes, feta, olives, €4–5
meals.dinner: Dinner in Megalochori or Pyrgos village — authentic local taverna with fewer tourists and lower prices, €9–11

day_by_day.notes: Renting a scooter requires a valid license. If uncomfortable on a scooter, rent an ATV instead — no license required in Greece for small ATVs, though always ride carefully on the winding island roads. Red Beach has a short rocky path to access — wear sturdy shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Oia village in the morning (before the crowds arrive). Explore the iconic blue-domed churches, white-washed buildings, and narrow alleyways. Photography is stunning in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the famous caldera trail from Oia back toward Fira (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) — one of the most scenic hikes in Greece with breathtaking views the entire way. Alternatively, take the bus back and relax at Kamari beach.
day_by_day.evening: If you did the hike, you'll arrive back in Fira in time for the famous Oia sunset (take the bus back up). Join the crowds at Oia's castle ruins for the legendary Santorini sunset — arrive 1 hour early for a good spot.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before heading to Oia — coffee and tiropita, €2.50
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the hike or stop at a small cafe along the trail — sandwich and water, €4–6
meals.dinner: Farewell Santorini dinner — treat yourself slightly with a meal at a mid-range restaurant in Fira with caldera views, €15–18. Order the local white wine (Assyrtiko) — Santorini's famous grape variety.

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia caldera hike is moderately challenging. Wear good shoes, bring plenty of water (2+ liters), sunscreen, and a hat. Start early to avoid the worst of the midday heat. The trail is well-marked.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Santorini. Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira (€6) to see artifacts from the Akrotiri excavations, including stunning Minoan frescoes. Then do any last-minute shopping — local products like Santorini wine, fava, and capers make great budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the afternoon high-speed ferry back to Piraeus/Athens (book in advance for best prices — €40–55 economy). Enjoy the sea views and relax on the journey back.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Athens (Piraeus) in the evening. Take the Metro back to central Athens. Check into your Athens accommodation for the final night. Take a nostalgic last walk through Monastiraki and Plaka.

meals.breakfast: Final Santorini breakfast — Greek yogurt with local honey and fresh fruit at a cafe, €4–5
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or pack snacks — sandwiches and local snacks bought from a mini-market, €4–6
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — revisit your favorite taverna from Day 2 or try something new in Psiri. Budget €10–12 for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book your return ferry well in advance, especially for summer travel. High-speed ferries (SeaJets, Hellenic Seaways) are faster but pricier than conventional ferries — balance cost vs. time. Keep your transit card topped up for the Metro from Piraeus.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Revisit any sites you missed or simply enjoy a slow Greek breakfast at a neighborhood cafe. Visit the Zappeion Gardens or the National Garden (free) for a peaceful green escape in the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Monastiraki flea market — pick up olive oil, herbs, local honey, or handmade ceramics at reasonable prices. Head to the airport with plenty of time (allow 2–3 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, ancient history, and incredible Greek food!

meals.breakfast: Slow final Greek breakfast — freddo espresso (iced coffee), koulouri, and a cheese pie at a traditional kafeneio, €3–4
meals.lunch: Last souvlaki wrap in Athens — the perfect budget farewell meal, €2.50–3.50
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Athens Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) is connected to the city center by Metro Line 3 (Blue Line) — journey takes about 40 minutes and costs €9. Allow extra time for check-in and security. Use any remaining euros on last food or souvenirs at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens (approx. 40–60 min). Check into your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Syntagma area. Freshen up and take a gentle stroll around Monastiraki Square to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Plaka neighborhood, exploring the narrow pedestrian streets beneath the Acropolis. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner at a traditional taverna on the hillside.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or spanakopita from a street kiosk near the airport or upon arrival in the city center (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Taverna tou Psarra in Plaka — try grilled octopus, tzatziki, and a carafe of house wine. Budget approx. €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Buy an Ath.ena transit card at the airport Metro station for convenient travel throughout your stay. Exchange some cash or use ATMs in the arrivals hall.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis (open from 8:00 AM) before the crowds and heat build up. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and the Propylaea. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Book tickets online in advance to skip queues (€20 standard entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill — one of Europe's finest archaeological museums with stunning glass-floor galleries (€10 entry). Afterward, head to the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street to browse fresh produce, spices, olives, and local cheeses.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Piraeus by Metro (Line 1, approx. 25 min) for the featured experience: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor. Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna sampling fresh grilled fish, shrimp saganaki, and local white wine while watching fishing boats bob in the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, freddo espresso (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch near the Central Market — stuffed vine leaves, fava dip, and fresh bread at a local ouzeri (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor, Piraeus — fresh catch of the day, grilled calamari, Greek salad. Budget €28–38 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Acropolis — the marble paths are uneven and slippery. Bring sunscreen and a hat; temperatures around 23°C can feel hotter in direct sun on the hill. The Mikrolimano harbor area is beautiful at sunset — aim to arrive around 7:30–8:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Syntagma Square to watch the Evzone guard change ceremony at the Hellenic Parliament (full ceremony on the hour, grand ceremony on Sundays). Walk through the National Garden — a peaceful green oasis in the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood and visit the Benaki Museum of Greek Culture (€9 entry) — excellent collection spanning ancient to modern Greek history. Browse the museum's rooftop café for views over Athens.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Psiri and Gazi neighborhoods for Athens' lively bar and restaurant scene. Enjoy dinner at a modern Greek restaurant blending traditional recipes with contemporary presentation.

meals.breakfast: Café in Syntagma area — tiropita (cheese pie), koulouri sesame bread ring, and Greek coffee (€4–7)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Benaki Museum rooftop café — light salads, sandwiches, and fresh juices with Acropolis views (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Psiri — try Nolan or a similar modern taverna for creative Greek dishes like slow-cooked lamb with orzo or grilled sea bream. Budget €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Benaki Museum is closed on Tuesdays — Wednesday through Monday is fine. Kolonaki is a great area for people-watching and window shopping. Gazi comes alive after 9 PM if you want to experience Athens' nightlife.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens for Santorini — take a high-speed ferry from Piraeus port (approx. 5–5.5 hours, book with Hellenic Seaways or SeaJets, €45–65 per person). Enjoy the Aegean scenery from the deck. Arrive in Santorini's Athinios port and transfer to your accommodation in Fira or Imerovigli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and settle into your Santorini accommodation (mid-range cave hotel or boutique guesthouse in Fira, approx. €80–120/night). Explore Fira town on foot — the main caldera-edge walkway, the Orthodox Cathedral, and the Archaeological Museum of Thera (€6 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk the famous caldera path from Fira toward Imerovigli (approx. 3 km, 1 hour) for spectacular sunset views over the caldera. Return to Fira for dinner at a caldera-view restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Athens hotel before departure, or grab pastries and coffee at Piraeus port (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Lunch on the ferry — pack snacks or buy from the onboard café (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira at a mid-range caldera-view taverna — fava santorinis (yellow split pea dip), tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and grilled local fish. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets at least 2–3 days in advance, especially for June travel. The high-speed catamaran is more comfortable but pricier than the standard ferry. Santorini's Athinios port is at the base of steep cliffs — take the bus or taxi up to Fira (do not attempt the donkey path with luggage). Fira is the island's capital and a great central base.

day_by_day.morning: Rent an ATV or scooter (€20–30/day) and head to the iconic village of Oia in the north of the island. Explore the blue-domed churches, whitewashed alleys, and art galleries. Visit the Venetian Castle ruins for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to Perissa or Perivolos Beach — Santorini's famous black volcanic sand beaches on the eastern coast. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the unique black sand experience. Sun loungers and umbrellas available for rent (€8–12 for a set).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the world-famous Santorini sunset — arrive by 7:00 PM to secure a good viewing spot as it gets very crowded. Afterward, enjoy dinner in Oia.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a café in Fira — Greek yogurt parfait, fresh orange juice, and coffee (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perissa — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer. Budget €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Oia — try Roka or a similar local restaurant for fresh seafood pasta, grilled octopus, and local Assyrtiko white wine. Budget €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset — consider watching from the Skaros Rock near Imerovigli for a less crowded but equally stunning view. Apply high-SPF sunscreen; the Aegean sun reflects off white buildings intensely. The black sand beaches get very hot — bring water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat tour of the Santorini caldera (book through your hotel or at the port, €25–40 per person). Visit the active volcanic island of Nea Kameni, hike to the crater, and swim in the warm sulfuric hot springs of Palea Kameni.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean' (€12 entry). Afterward, relax at the nearby Red Beach, one of Santorini's most dramatic and photogenic beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira for a relaxed evening. Browse the local shops along the caldera walkway and enjoy a sundowner cocktail at a caldera-view bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before the boat tour (included or €8–12 at a nearby café)
meals.lunch: Lunch near Akrotiri village — a simple local taverna serving moussaka, stuffed peppers, and fresh bread (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira — try Metaxy Mas for authentic Santorinian cuisine: white eggplant salad, local capers, and slow-cooked beef with pasta. Budget €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The caldera boat tour typically departs from Fira's old port (accessible by cable car, €6 round trip, or 580 steps on foot). Wear sturdy shoes for the Nea Kameni volcanic hike — the terrain is rough. Red Beach requires a short rocky walk from the parking area — wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (approx. 2–3 hours by high-speed ferry, €35–55 per person). Enjoy the island-hopping experience across the Cyclades. Arrive in Mykonos New Port and transfer to your accommodation in Mykonos Town (Chora).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) on foot — get wonderfully lost in the labyrinthine whitewashed alleys designed to confuse pirates. Visit the iconic windmills on the Kato Mili hill, the charming Little Venice waterfront neighborhood, and the Paraportiani Church.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Mykonos' famous sunset from the Little Venice area, where the colorful balconied houses hang directly over the sea. The area has numerous bars and cafés perfect for sundowners.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before ferry departure — grab a cheese pie and coffee from a Fira bakery (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Mykonos Town upon arrival — fresh souvlaki wrap or a mezze plate at a harbor-side café (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Mykonos Town — try M-eating or a similar quality mid-range restaurant for fresh lobster pasta, grilled sea bass, and local wine. Budget €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos accommodation is pricier than other islands — book a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel in Chora well in advance (€90–140/night). The town's alleyways are intentionally confusing — use your phone's GPS or simply enjoy getting lost. Mykonos is known for its party scene but also has quieter, more authentic corners.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short boat excursion to the sacred island of Delos (30 min from Mykonos Old Port, €20 round trip + €12 site entry). One of the most important archaeological sites in Greece — birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, with remarkably preserved ancient ruins including the famous Terrace of the Lions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and head to one of the island's beautiful beaches. Platis Gialos is a good mid-range option with calm waters and beach facilities. Alternatively, Agios Sostis is quieter and more natural. Rent a scooter or take the local bus (€2).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Explore the Matogianni Street shopping area and enjoy dinner at a waterfront restaurant in the Old Port area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a Chora café — scrambled eggs, fresh tomatoes, olives, and Greek coffee (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Platis Gialos — grilled fish, Greek salad, and fresh lemonade. Budget €16–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a taverna near the Old Port — fresh grilled octopus, shrimp with ouzo, and a shared mezze spread. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port (not the New Port) at 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM, returning at 12:00 PM and 1:30 PM. The site has no shade — bring a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water. Delos is closed on Mondays, so Tuesday is perfect. The island has no accommodation or restaurants — bring snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the quieter, more authentic side of Mykonos — rent a scooter and drive to the traditional village of Ano Mera in the island's interior. Visit the 16th-century Panagia Tourliani Monastery with its ornate marble fountain and icon collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Elia Beach — Mykonos' longest beach on the southeastern coast, with crystal-clear water and a more relaxed atmosphere than the famous party beaches. Swim, snorkel, and relax. Sun loungers available (€10–15 for a set).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final evening in Mykonos Town. Take a cooking class or simply enjoy a leisurely dinner and the famous Mykonos nightlife atmosphere (without necessarily staying out all night).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Chora — fresh fruit, yogurt, honey, and freddo cappuccino (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beach taverna at Elia — fresh catch, tzatziki, and cold beer. Budget €18–24 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell Mykonos dinner — try Kounelas Fish Tavern in the Old Port for no-frills, excellent fresh fish by the kilo. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Elia Beach is accessible by local bus from Mykonos Town (€2) or by water taxi from Platis Gialos. The beach has a mix of straight and LGBTQ+ sections — all are welcoming. Pack your bags tonight as you'll be heading to Crete tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry from Mykonos to Heraklion, Crete (approx. 4–5 hours, €35–50 per person). Arrive in Heraklion and check into your mid-range hotel. Head immediately to the Palace of Knossos (5 km from city center, bus or taxi) — the legendary Minoan palace complex dating to 1700 BC (€15 entry). Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Heraklion city center and visit the excellent Heraklion Archaeological Museum — home to the world's finest collection of Minoan artifacts including the famous Phaistos Disc and Bull's Head Rhyton (€10 entry). Walk along the Venetian harbor and the impressive Koules Fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Lion Square (Plateia Venizelou) area and the surrounding streets for dinner. Heraklion has a fantastic local food scene that's less touristy than the islands.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before ferry — pastry and coffee at Mykonos port (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Knossos — a local taverna serving dakos (Cretan rusk salad), fresh cheese, and cold water (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Heraklion's old town — try Peskesi for authentic Cretan cuisine: snails in vinegar, lamb with stamnagathi greens, and aged graviera cheese. Budget €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Knossos is best visited in the morning before the tour groups arrive. The site is partially reconstructed — controversial among archaeologists but visually impressive. Heraklion is Crete's capital and a real working city — a refreshing contrast to the tourist-heavy islands. The Venetian harbor area is beautiful for an evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a car in Heraklion (€35–50/day) and drive west along the northern coast to the charming Venetian harbor town of Chania (approx. 2 hours). Explore the stunning old harbor with its Egyptian lighthouse, Venetian arsenals, and the covered market on Skrydlof Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south from Chania to the famous Elafonisi Beach (approx. 1.5 hours) — a stunning lagoon with pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise water. Swim and relax in one of Greece's most beautiful beach settings. Return to Chania for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Chania's old harbor area — one of the most romantic dining settings in all of Greece, with restaurants lining the waterfront beneath the Venetian lighthouse.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Heraklion hotel or a café before departure (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Elafonisi — buy supplies at a Chania market: local bread, olives, cheese, and fruit (€8–12 total)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a waterfront taverna in Chania's old harbor — fresh grilled fish, Cretan salad with local olive oil, and a carafe of local wine. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Consider staying overnight in Chania rather than returning to Heraklion — Chania is arguably the most beautiful town in Crete and deserves more time. Mid-range guesthouses in the old town run €70–110/night. Elafonisi can get crowded by midday in June — arrive before noon. The drive through the White Mountains (Lefka Ori) is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest gorges at 16 km (allow 4–6 hours). The trail descends from the Omalos plateau through dramatic scenery to the coastal village of Agia Roumeli. Buses depart from Chania to the trailhead at 6:15 AM, 7:30 AM, and 8:30 AM (€2.50 each way). Entry fee €5.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Agia Roumeli at the gorge's end — a tiny village accessible only by boat or on foot. Swim in the crystal-clear Libyan Sea to soothe tired muscles. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (€15, approx. 1 hour) and then bus back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania by late afternoon. Enjoy a well-deserved relaxing evening — a soak, a massage if available at your hotel, and a leisurely dinner celebrating the gorge hike.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before the bus — energy-rich foods: eggs, bread, cheese, and coffee (€6–9). Pack extra snacks and 2+ liters of water for the hike.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the taverna in Agia Roumeli after completing the gorge — grilled meat, salad, and cold drinks. Budget €14–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner in Chania old town — try Well of the Turk for a unique Cretan-Ottoman fusion menu in a historic setting. Budget €22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge is strenuous — wear proper hiking shoes (not sandals), bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and snacks. The gorge is one-way (top to bottom only). The ferry and bus connections from Agia Roumeli are the only way back — check the last ferry time (usually 5:30–6:00 PM). The gorge is closed in winter and after heavy rain — June conditions should be ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Crete — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and a last stroll through Chania's old town and harbor. Visit the Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Collection of Chania (€2 entry) housed in a beautiful Venetian church. Browse the leather goods and local products on Skrydlof Street for souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Heraklion (or Chania airport if flying from there) for your return journey. Allow extra time for car return and check-in. If time permits before departure, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a harbor café.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Heraklion International Airport (HER) or Chania International Airport (CHQ) for your return flight. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of Greek beaches, ancient history, and incredible local food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — Cretan honey, fresh yogurt, local cheese, and strong coffee at a Chania café (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch before departure — a final souvlaki wrap or a Cretan dakos salad at a harbor café (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal — pick up some local snacks (thyme honey, dried herbs, local cheese) to bring home as edible souvenirs.

day_by_day.notes: Heraklion airport is about 5 km from the city center (15 min by taxi, €15–18). Chania airport is 15 km from the city (25 min by taxi, €25–30). Return your rental car with a full tank to avoid surcharges. Greece has a strict 3-bag-per-person rule on domestic ferries — check airline baggage allowances for your return flight. Consider buying local products at the airport duty-free: Cretan olive oil, Santorini wine, and Greek honey make excellent gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

experiences.name: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market where you can taste local cheeses, olives, cured meats, spices, and fresh produce alongside locals. A guided or self-guided walk through the stalls offers an authentic culinary immersion away from the heat.

experiences.name: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach
experiences.description: Visit the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon and evening when temperatures drop. Swim in the crystal-clear waters of the Saronic Gulf, enjoy sunbeds, and watch the spectacular Athenian Riviera sunset. Easily accessible from central Athens and close to quality seafood restaurants.

experiences.name: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine
experiences.description: Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district, learning to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and tzatziki from scratch. Classes run in the evening to avoid heat, and you enjoy your creations as dinner afterward.

experiences.name: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island
experiences.description: Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon, avoiding peak heat. Swim at the calm, clear beaches near Aegina Town, try the island's famous pistachio products and fresh fish at a harbor taverna, and return by evening ferry. A full island experience within budget and close to Athens.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your hotel in the Athens/Piraeus area. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the waterfront promenade to begin soaking in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor — Dine at a traditional upscale waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus. Sample freshly caught seafood including grilled octopus, sea bream, and prawns saganaki, paired with crisp Assyrtiko white wine, while watching the yachts bob in the harbor under the warm June evening sky.

meals.breakfast: Served on the flight or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or en route from the airport
meals.dinner: Upscale seafood taverna at Mikrolimano Harbor, Piraeus — expect to spend €80–€120 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance. Mikrolimano is only a short drive from Piraeus hotels. June evenings are warm (~18–20°C) and perfect for outdoor harbor dining. Confirm restaurant reservation before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour — Begin your morning with an immersive guided tour of the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market). Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, cured meats, olives, spices, and local cheeses. Taste your way through the market with a knowledgeable local guide who will explain the cultural significance of each ingredient and introduce you to vendors who have worked there for generations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for a leisurely afternoon. Visit the Benaki Museum for a curated look at Greek art and history, then browse the boutique shops and galleries along Tsakalof and Skoufa streets. Enjoy a refreshing Greek frappe or specialty coffee at one of Kolonaki's stylish cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine — Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a beautifully appointed kitchen in the Plaka district. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as spanakopita, moussaka, tzatziki, and loukoumades under the guidance of a professional Greek chef. Sit down to enjoy the full meal you've prepared, paired with selected Greek wines.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious hotel breakfast buffet featuring Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, fresh pastries, cold cuts, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch at a premium taverna in Monastiraki — try dakos, taramosalata, and grilled halloumi
meals.dinner: The dishes you prepare during the cooking class in Plaka, paired with curated Greek wines (class typically includes full dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance as small-group sessions fill quickly. The Athens Central Market is best visited before noon when it is most vibrant. Wear comfortable shoes for the market tour.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Acropolis and Parthenon — Beat the midday heat and crowds with an early-morning private tour starting at 8:00 AM. A licensed archaeologist guide will bring the history of ancient Athens to life as you explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and the stunning Propylaea. Finish with a visit to the world-class Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach — Take a private car to the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni on the Athens Riviera. Arrive in the early afternoon to claim a premium sun lounger and umbrella. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters of the Saronic Gulf, enjoy a beach cocktail service, and relax as the temperature softens toward evening.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant along the Athens Riviera — dine at one of the sophisticated seafront restaurants near Vouliagmeni or Glyfada, enjoying grilled whole fish, lobster pasta, and local wines with sea views as the sun sets over the Saronic Gulf.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt parfait, smoked salmon, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and artisan bread
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at Vouliagmeni's upscale beach club — fresh salads, grilled calamari, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Premium seafront restaurant on the Athens Riviera near Vouliagmeni — budget €100–€150 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and private guide well in advance. Vouliagmeni Beach charges an entry fee for sun lounger service; premium spots should be reserved. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — June sun is strong even at 23°C.

day_by_day.morning: Late morning departure by high-speed ferry from Piraeus to Mykonos. Opt for a business-class cabin or premium deck seating on a Hellenic Seaways or SeaJets high-speed catamaran (approximately 2.5–3.5 hours). Enjoy the sea breeze and views of the Cycladic islands as you approach Mykonos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Mykonos and transfer to your luxury hotel (recommend a clifftop or seafront property in Agios Ioannis or Ornos area). After check-in, spend the afternoon exploring the iconic whitewashed lanes of Mykonos Town (Chora) — discover the famous windmills, Little Venice, and the charming Church of Paraportiani. Browse high-end boutiques and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Little Venice, Mykonos Town — enjoy cocktails at sunset from a terrace overlooking the Aegean, followed by a refined dinner featuring Cycladic cuisine: fresh lobster, sea urchin pasta, and local Mykonian sausage, paired with an excellent Santorini Assyrtiko.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure or a pastry and coffee at a Piraeus café near the port
meals.lunch: Onboard the ferry — light snacks, or a quick mezze at a portside café upon arrival in Mykonos
meals.dinner: Upscale Little Venice restaurant, Mykonos Town — €120–€180 per person with premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book high-speed ferry tickets well in advance for June travel. Confirm luxury hotel reservation in Mykonos. Mykonos Town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable sandals. June is peak season; restaurant reservations are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion around Mykonos — Charter a private speedboat or sailing yacht for a half-day morning trip. Visit the secluded sea caves and hidden coves on the island's southern coast, snorkel in pristine waters, and stop at the uninhabited islet of Dragonisi to swim in its famous sea caves. The crew will provide chilled drinks and light snacks on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at one of Mykonos's premium beach clubs — Nammos at Psarou Beach or Scorpios at Paraga offer world-class service, crystal-clear water, and a glamorous atmosphere. Enjoy a sun lounger with full table service, refreshing cocktails, and a light Mediterranean lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Mykonos Town, followed by a late dinner at a top-rated Mykonian restaurant. Try fresh grilled fish, Cycladic cheese plates, and handmade pasta with local seafood, accompanied by a curated Greek wine list.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — fresh fruit platters, eggs Benedict, Greek pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch at Nammos or Scorpios — fresh salads, sushi, grilled seafood, and rosé
meals.dinner: Top-rated Mykonian restaurant in Chora — €130–€200 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charters should be booked at least 2–3 days in advance. Psarou Beach (Nammos) is extremely popular — reserve sun loungers ahead. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the sacred island of Delos — Take the short boat from Mykonos Town (30 minutes) to the UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site of Delos, one of the most important mythological and historical sites in Greece. Explore the ancient ruins of the Sanctuary of Apollo, the Terrace of the Lions, and the remarkably preserved mosaics of the House of Dionysus with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos by early afternoon. Relax at your hotel's pool or private beach. Alternatively, visit the quieter, more authentic beach of Agios Sostis on the northern coast — no beach clubs, just natural beauty, golden sand, and turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Mykonos — choose an intimate, candlelit restaurant in the backstreets of Chora for a refined final evening on the island. Enjoy a tasting menu featuring the best of Cycladic cuisine: fresh ceviche, grilled langoustines, and a honey-and-walnut dessert, paired with aged Vinsanto wine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked salmon bagels, Greek yogurt with thyme honey, fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a traditional taverna near Agios Sostis beach — grilled fish, village salad, and local wine
meals.dinner: Intimate fine-dining restaurant in Mykonos Chora — tasting menu €150–€220 per person with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port of Mykonos Town — check schedules as they are limited. The site has no shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen, and water. Delos is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Morning ferry from Mykonos to Santorini — board a high-speed catamaran (approximately 2 hours). Enjoy the spectacular approach to Santorini's caldera from the sea — one of the most dramatic arrivals in the world. Transfer to your luxury hotel in Oia or Imerovigli (recommend a cave suite or infinity-pool villa with caldera views).
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — wander the narrow cobblestone paths, admire the blue-domed churches, browse the art galleries and jewelry boutiques, and take in the breathtaking caldera views. Visit the Venetian castle ruins for a panoramic perspective of the island.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset in Oia — one of the world's most celebrated sunsets. Secure a premium spot at a caldera-view restaurant or your hotel's terrace well before sunset. Enjoy champagne or a Santorini Assyrtiko cocktail as the sun melts into the Aegean. Follow with dinner at a top caldera-view restaurant in Oia.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the ferry or at a café in Mykonos port before departure
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch at a caldera-view café in Oia — fava dip, cherry tomato bruschetta, and local wine
meals.dinner: Premium caldera-view restaurant in Oia — fresh lobster, grilled sea bass, and Santorini wine — €140–€200 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your Santorini luxury hotel well in advance — June is peak season and the best cave suites sell out months ahead. The Oia sunset draws large crowds; your hotel terrace may offer a more exclusive experience. Ferry tickets should be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sailing tour of the Santorini caldera — embark on a luxury private catamaran from Ammoudi Bay or Vlychada Marina. Sail around the volcanic islands of Nea Kameni and Palea Kameni, swim in the warm sulfuric hot springs, snorkel in the crystal-clear caldera waters, and enjoy a gourmet breakfast and Champagne on deck with views of the iconic white cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' A private guide will bring this extraordinary site to life. Afterward, relax at the famous Red Beach nearby — a dramatic landscape of red and black volcanic rock meeting turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Fira or Firostefani — enjoy a sophisticated menu of Santorinian specialties: white eggplant salad, fava with capers, fresh tuna tartare, and grilled octopus, paired with an exceptional local wine flight featuring Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast served on the private catamaran — fresh fruit, pastries, smoked salmon, and Champagne
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a taverna near Akrotiri or Red Beach — grilled fish and village salad
meals.dinner: Fine-dining restaurant in Fira or Firostefani with caldera views — €130–€190 per person with wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran tours typically run 5–6 hours and should be booked in advance. Akrotiri has an entry fee and is best visited with a guide. Red Beach requires a short walk over rocky terrain — wear sturdy sandals.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting tour of Santorini's volcanic vineyards — visit two or three of the island's most prestigious wineries, such as Santo Wines, Domaine Sigalas, or Hatzidakis. Learn about the unique basket-trained vine cultivation method (kouloura) that protects vines from the Aegean winds. Taste a curated selection of Assyrtiko, Athiri, and Aidani wines alongside local cheese and charcuterie pairings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the traditional village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest point and one of its most authentic, less-touristy villages. Wander through medieval Venetian castle ruins, visit the Church of Christ, and enjoy panoramic 360-degree views of the entire island. Stop for a traditional Greek coffee at a local kafeneion.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at your hotel's infinity pool overlooking the caldera, followed by a private in-suite dinner or a reservation at one of Santorini's most exclusive restaurants — consider a chef's table experience or a tasting menu at a Michelin-recommended establishment in Oia.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — eggs any style, fresh-squeezed juices, Greek pastries, and local honey
meals.lunch: Wine and cheese pairing at the winery, supplemented by a light mezze plate
meals.dinner: Chef's table or tasting menu at a top Santorini restaurant — €180–€280 per person with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for the winery tour as roads can be narrow and wine tasting is involved. Book the chef's table experience well in advance — these are extremely limited and popular. Pyrgos is best explored in the late afternoon when light is golden.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at leisure — enjoy a late breakfast at your hotel, take a dip in your private pool, and soak in the caldera views. Alternatively, take a morning hike along the scenic caldera trail from Fira to Oia (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) — one of the most spectacular walks in Greece, with uninterrupted views of the volcanic landscape and Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Perissa and Perivolos beaches on Santorini's southeastern coast — famous for their dramatic black volcanic sand. Settle into a premium beach club with full sun lounger service, swim in the warm June waters, and enjoy a leisurely afternoon of relaxation. The black sand retains heat beautifully, creating a unique beach experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Santorini — enjoy a romantic sunset dinner at a cliffside restaurant in Imerovigli, considered by many to offer even more dramatic caldera views than Oia. Indulge in a full seafood feast: oysters, grilled langoustines, whole baked sea bream, and a bottle of aged Assyrtiko.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full spread with local specialties including Santorinian tomato fritters (tomatokeftedes)
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch at Perivolos — fresh seafood, salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Cliffside fine-dining restaurant in Imerovigli — full seafood tasting menu, €150–€220 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia hike is best started early morning to avoid midday heat. Wear proper walking shoes and bring plenty of water. Black sand beaches get very hot — beach shoes are recommended. Book the Imerovigli dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning ferry or short flight from Santorini back to Athens. Arrive in Athens by midday and transfer via private car to your hotel. Freshen up and enjoy a leisurely late morning exploring the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood — visit the Cycladic Art Museum for a world-class collection of ancient Cycladic figurines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island — Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina (approximately 40 minutes). Explore the charming port town, visit the impressive Temple of Aphaia (one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples), and browse the famous pistachio stalls — Aegina is renowned for producing Greece's finest pistachios. Enjoy the relaxed, authentic island atmosphere away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Piraeus by early evening and enjoy a final Athens dinner at a premium restaurant in the Monastiraki or Psyrri neighborhood — a sophisticated setting with views of the illuminated Acropolis. Enjoy modern Greek cuisine: lamb chops with herb crust, grilled sea bass with lemon-caper sauce, and a selection of artisan Greek cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the Santorini hotel or airport before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a waterfront taverna in Aegina Town — fresh grilled fish, pistachio salad, and local wine
meals.dinner: Premium modern Greek restaurant in Monastiraki or Psyrri with Acropolis views — €100–€160 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm ferry or flight from Santorini to Athens well in advance. The Aegina ferry departs regularly from Piraeus — check the afternoon schedule. Buy Aegina pistachios as premium gifts or souvenirs — they are exceptional quality.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the National Archaeological Museum of Athens — one of the world's greatest museums of ancient art. A private guide will lead you through the highlights: the Mask of Agamemnon, the Antikythera Mechanism, the stunning bronze statue of Poseidon, and the extraordinary Minoan frescoes from Akrotiri. Allow 2.5–3 hours for a thorough, unhurried visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon in the vibrant Pangrati and Mets neighborhoods — Athens's most authentic residential districts. Visit the Panathenaic Stadium (Kallimarmaro), the only stadium in the world built entirely of marble and the site of the first modern Olympic Games in 1896. Stroll through the National Garden for a peaceful green escape in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner in Athens — reserve a table at one of Athens's finest restaurants, such as Spondi (two Michelin stars) or Varoulko Seaside. Enjoy a full tasting menu celebrating the very best of Greek gastronomy — from Aegean seafood to aged Greek cheeses and exceptional wines — as a grand finale to your Greek journey.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — full spread with fresh pastries, eggs, smoked fish, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a premium café or brasserie near the National Garden — grilled chicken souvlaki, Greek salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred or top-rated Athens restaurant — full tasting menu with wine pairing, €200–€350 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the National Archaeological Museum private guide in advance. Spondi and Varoulko require reservations weeks ahead during peak season. The Panathenaic Stadium has an entry fee and offers an audio guide. Dress smartly for the fine-dining farewell dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at your hotel. Take a final stroll through the Plaka neighborhood, pick up last-minute premium souvenirs (extra virgin olive oil, aged balsamic from Kalamata, saffron from Kozani, or handmade ceramics), and enjoy a final Greek coffee at a traditional kafeneion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer via private luxury car to Athens International Airport for your departure flight. Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and duty-free shopping — the airport has an excellent selection of Greek products including wines, olive oils, and local delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens — carry with you the memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring Greece's beaches, flavors, ancient history, and island magic.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious hotel breakfast — savor every last bite of Greek yogurt, thyme honey, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a final quick bite at a café in Plaka before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in during peak June travel season. Athens airport traffic can be heavy — confirm transfer timing with your concierge. Keep premium food souvenirs in checked luggage if over 100ml liquid restrictions apply.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
